basic_identification.full_title: Multi-Function Valve Assembly for Permanently Fixed Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Containers for Automotive Use — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Divisional Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the materials, design, construction, and testing requirements for multi-function valve assemblies of both liquid and vapour withdrawal types intended for permanently fixed type liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) containers for automotive use. It is designed to ensure that the safety levels currently existing for other automotive pressure fittings are strictly maintained.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: According to the product standard text, certification is permissive: conforming valve assemblies 'may also be marked' with the Standard Mark under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986. While the mark itself is permissive, the code introduces strict statutory testing requirements, periodic retesting schedules, and mandatory marking/warning criteria.

requirements.provision: The multi-function valve may also be marked with the Standard Mark under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder.

It is the responsibility of owners and users to ensure that the multi-function valve assembly is periodically tested as per norms laid down in the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004, as amended from time-to-time and as enforced by statutory authorities.

The valve body and service valve body must be forged from wrought or extruded sections, meeting minimum mechanical criteria (tensile strength of at least 392 N/mm² and Izod impact strength of at least 21.5 N.m) verified by batch testing.

Each multi-function valve body and filler connector must be permanently and legibly marked with the manufacturer's identification mark, model number, specification number, maximum working pressure (2 MPa), mounting angle & auto LPG tank diameter/height, quarter & year of manufacture, PRV flow rate, and inspector's mark.

All integrated electrical sub-components must pass strict safety certifications, including an electrical overvoltage test (withstanding 1.5 times the rated voltage for 3 minutes) and an insulation resistance test (withstanding 1,000 V d.c. for at least 2 seconds with minimum resistance of 240 kΩ).

Type approval requires a mandatory schedule of performance and durability tests, including withstanding 6,000 opening/closing cycles (for the service valve, excess-flow valve, and PRV), 6,000 complete filling cycles (for the automatic fill limiter), a type-approval bonfire test, and exhaustive 3-axis resonance vibration tests.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15100:2018 is the national standard specification in India for multi-function valve assemblies mounted on permanently fixed automotive LPG containers (covering both liquid and vapour withdrawal systems). Designed to maintain high safety levels equivalent to other automotive pressure fittings, this standard regulates vital components including the automatic 80 percent fill limiter, remotely controlled service valve, excess flow check valve, pressure relief valve, fusible plug, and indirect contents gauge. When specifying or inspecting these systems, engineers must verify that the forged valve bodies satisfy mandatory tensile and impact tests, that elastomers withstand strict LPG swelling and temperature aging limits, that electrical components meet insulation and overvoltage safety clearances, and that the complete assembly successfully undergoes the 6,000-cycle endurance test, 3-axis vibration test, and bonfire test.
